issues.label: DVPA relationship qualifies
issues.why: The court must confirm the parties are within DVPA’s covered relationships (dating/cohabiting).

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction and notice
issues.why: The court must ensure proper service/notice and personal jurisdiction over each party before issuing orders.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must have DVPA authority to adjudicate and issue the requested restraints.

issues.label: Venue and proper forum
issues.why: The court must confirm the proceeding is properly filed in the correct county/court division.

issues.label: Mootness or changed circumstances
issues.why: The court must consider whether cessation of contact before filing/hearing undermines need for prospective relief.

issues.label: Evidentiary hearing fairness
issues.why: The court must provide each side a meaningful opportunity to present relevant evidence and be heard.

issues.label: Self-represented party safeguards
issues.why: The court must manage the hearing to avoid unfairness to the self-represented litigant while remaining neutral.

issues.label: Improper time-limiting relevance
issues.why: The court must not exclude relevant history that bears on current fear, credibility, or likelihood of future abuse.

issues.label: Consider entire relationship history
issues.why: Past abuse during the relationship can be highly probative of whether future abuse is reasonably likely.

issues.label: Define “abuse” under DVPA
issues.why: The court must apply DVPA’s definition of abuse, including disturbing the peace and coercive control-like conduct.

issues.label: Disturbing the peace standard
issues.why: The court must decide if conduct (including indirect contact) destroyed the other’s mental or emotional calm.

issues.label: Harassment and stalking conduct
issues.why: The court must determine whether repeated unwanted contact and appearances constitute DVPA abuse and justify restraint.

issues.label: Threats and intimidation
issues.why: The court must evaluate alleged threats (e.g., gun photo text) and intimidation as abuse under DVPA.

issues.label: Sexual assault allegations
issues.why: The court must consider whether alleged coerced sex/sexual assault constitutes abuse supporting a DVRO.

issues.label: Physical abuse allegations
issues.why: The court must decide whether assaults, choking, restraint, and property destruction occurred and amount to DVPA abuse.

issues.label: Breaking and entering evidence
issues.why: Alleged break-ins and forced entry may show abuse, threats, and need for stay-away orders.

issues.label: Property damage as abuse
issues.why: Smashed phone/broken door may constitute abuse and corroborate violence or intimidation.

issues.label: Indirect contact via social media
issues.why: The court must decide whether posts/usernames aimed at the other party are contact/harassment under DVPA.

issues.label: Doxxing and privacy violations
issues.why: Posting phone number or private images may be abuse (disturbing peace/harassment) and affect tailored orders.

issues.label: Encouraging suicide allegations
issues.why: Directing “please kill yourself” may be emotional abuse disturbing peace and relevant to DVRO necessity.

issues.label: Impersonation/unfair competition conduct
issues.why: Using a similar business handle (“.con”) may be harassment/defamation affecting DVPA “disturbing peace” analysis.

issues.label: Third-party contact as abuse
issues.why: Calls to mother/friend may be indirect harassment/contact intended to reach or distress the protected person.

issues.label: Mutual no-contact order effect
issues.why: The court must consider whether violating PCC’s no-contact order shows ongoing risk and supports DVPA relief.

issues.label: Cease-and-desist letter relevance
issues.why: A demand to stop contact can establish notice that contact is unwanted and support harassment findings.

issues.label: Prior TRO and dismissal effect
issues.why: The court must evaluate legal effect of earlier unserved TRO and dismissal on credibility, pattern, and relief.

issues.label: Primary aggressor analysis
issues.why: With cross-requests, the court must identify the primary aggressor under Fam. Code § 6305 if issuing mutual orders.

issues.label: Self-defense determination
issues.why: The court must decide whether any alleged violence was primarily defensive, affecting § 6305 and merits.

issues.label: Mutual DVRO prerequisites
issues.why: If issuing mutual orders, the court must make the specific findings required by § 6305 (not just “both at fault”).

issues.label: Credibility assessments required
issues.why: Conflicting narratives require explicit or implicit credibility determinations supported by the record.

issues.label: Corroboration and documentary exhibits
issues.why: The court must weigh photos, screenshots, neighbor statements, and admissions for authenticity and probative value.

issues.label: Authentication of digital evidence
issues.why: Screenshots/posts/texts must be sufficiently authenticated to be relied upon for findings.

issues.label: Hearsay and exceptions
issues.why: The court must address admissibility/weight of neighbor statements and third-party declarations under applicable rules.

issues.label: Police report and recantation
issues.why: The court must evaluate photographs and initial report versus later recantation for reliability and weight.

issues.label: Admissions against interest
issues.why: Statements like “I admit I don’t have self-control…I continue to harass” may be admissions supporting findings.

issues.label: Timing of abuse and recency
issues.why: The court must consider how recent conduct is, but also whether older conduct predicts future harm.

issues.label: Reasonable apprehension of future abuse
issues.why: DVRO issuance requires determining whether protection is needed to prevent future acts of abuse.

issues.label: Protected persons scope
issues.why: If R.M. seeks protection for family members, the court must determine if they qualify and need protection.

issues.label: Stay-away distances and locations
issues.why: The court must tailor distances/places (homes, school, work, PCC) based on evidence and feasibility.

issues.label: Firearms relinquishment implications
issues.why: If a DVRO issues, the court must address firearm prohibitions and relinquishment requirements if applicable.

issues.label: Duration of orders
issues.why: The court must decide the appropriate duration (up to 5 years) based on risk and proportionality.

issues.label: No-contact vs peaceful contact terms
issues.why: The court must decide whether to allow limited contact (e.g., for school) or impose strict no-contact.

issues.label: Orders against online conduct
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how to restrain online postings/impersonation consistent with DVPA and specificity.

issues.label: First Amendment considerations
issues.why: Restrictions on speech/social media must be narrowly tailored to unprotected harassment/threats and DVPA purposes.

issues.label: Prior restraint specificity
issues.why: Any speech-related restraints must be clear and specific to avoid unconstitutional vagueness/overbreadth.

issues.label: Defamation vs DVPA abuse
issues.why: The court must distinguish protected opinion/defamation claims from actionable DVPA “disturbing peace” harassment.

issues.label: Workplace/school safety concerns
issues.why: The court must consider evidence of fear for coworkers and campus interactions when tailoring protections.

issues.label: Drug use and mental health relevance
issues.why: Substance use/mental health may affect credibility, risk assessment, and likelihood of future abuse.

issues.label: Retaliatory filing possibility
issues.why: The court should consider whether either petition is strategic/retaliatory, relevant to credibility and § 6305.

issues.label: Bias from focusing on one side
issues.why: The court must avoid appearing to pre-judge by discounting one party’s allegations solely due to timing or stereotypes.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings on denial
issues.why: When denying A.G.’s DVRO, the court must apply correct legal standards to her evidence, not just note her contact.

issues.label: Consideration of respondent’s conduct post-breakup
issues.why: The court must evaluate R.M.’s alleged indirect contacts (posts, calls, impersonation) as potential ongoing abuse.

issues.label: Consideration of petitioner’s conduct post-breakup
issues.why: The court must evaluate A.G.’s repeated contacts/visits as abuse and as evidence of future risk.

issues.label: Mutuality of wrongdoing not determinative
issues.why: Even if both acted badly, the court must independently assess each request under DVPA standards.

issues.label: Protective order necessity vs punishment
issues.why: DVROs are preventive; the court must ensure relief is based on preventing future abuse, not punishing past conduct.

issues.label: Vagueness of restrained acts
issues.why: Orders must clearly define prohibited conduct (direct/indirect contact, social media, third-party contact).

issues.label: Interaction with PCC no-contact order
issues.why: The court must consider overlap/conflict with school administrative orders and craft consistent terms.

issues.label: Standard of proof applied
issues.why: The court must apply the correct DVPA standard (preponderance) to each alleged act of abuse.

issues.label: Record completeness for review
issues.why: The court must ensure exhibits/testimony are properly admitted and identified to support enforceable orders and appellate review.
